nonBlockingObservations.observation: The body disqualifier walks the selected body node. In the pinned Rust grammar an outer attribute is a preceding sibling of function_item, not a descendant of its body block: the corpus tree for #[test] fn test_foo() {} is attribute_item then function_item whose body is an empty block. A body such as #[attr] fn f() { let mut x = 1; x } therefore still renames the explicit let mut binding. An attribute_item or inner_attribute_item inside the block, including one on an inner item, does disqualify that body. This matches NE §6.3's body span, which is the block, and it is a recall limit on item-level attribute macros.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: No change for this unit. E2c should implement the walk on the body node. A later revision that wants item-level attribute macros inside the same recall limit can disqualify a body whose owner is immediately preceded by a contiguous run of attribute_item siblings.

findingResolution.resolution: line_terminators() sets significant on every row except rust. TOKEN_LAW keeps a CR/LF whitespace gap as one opensip:line-break token whose value is 0x0A, and L2_LAW replaces a non-directive comment that contains U+000A, U+000D, U+2028 or U+2029 with one line-break token, then merges consecutive line-break tokens. JSX text stays in the jsx_text token the pinned scanner emits; a JSX gap is newline-led indentation and becomes a line-break. The asi-return-newline and asi-comment-newline fixtures stay distinct at L1 and L2, and the r1 insignificant override collides again.

RUST_PATTERN_LAW binds only ref_pattern/identifier, mut_pattern/identifier, captured_pattern's first identifier, a let_declaration or parameter pattern that has mutable_specifier, and a field_pattern name with mutable_specifier or the anonymous ref token. Those are the shapes in tree-sitter-rust v0.24.2. Every other identifier in a pattern is an ambiguous pattern identifier, binds nothing, and is non-renamable under R4. statedLimit records the declares and L3 recall loss. The same pattern law feeds declares.

token_tree is in RUST_ATOMIC, so a macro token tree is one exact-byte token at L1 through L3. The macro-token-tree-atomic fixture keeps (left /*one*/ right) distinct from (left /*two*/ right) at L2, and removing token_tree from atomic kinds reproduces the r1 collision. bodyDisqualifiers are a use_wildcard, any macro_invocation, and any attribute_item or inner_attribute_item in the body. The visible-name and format-capture guards are gone from disqualifying.

CONTROL_FLOW_LAW states List with and without a field, and selection uses only the role tables: Rust expression_statement reads fields on its expression child, an else_clause alternative is replaced by its first named non-nonStatements child, a selected statementLists node is transparent, any other selected node is one flow node, and opacity wins over a role. The Rust unsafe_block role is removed. switch_case lists only its body field. try reads the body field of the catch_clause in handler and of the finally_clause in finalizer, which are the fields in the pinned JavaScript grammar.

enter(X) goes to the first flow node of a posttest loop's body, and every edge target passes through enter except the body's end and a continue, which reach the test. The test's true edge is branch-true back to the body and its false edge leaves. The cf-do-while graph enters at the if, sends continue and the end of work() to the do_statement, and sends the test's false edge to after().

P is the owner's container chain plus the owner's own segment. entry and exit are P/entry:@0 and P/exit:@0. Flow-node ordinals count inside that graph. The two-function fixture gives syntax:a.js#function:f@0/... and syntax:a.js#function:g@0/.... The checker reproduces the r1 collision under a strict-ancestor prefix.

L3_LAW Resolution says a binding-site occurrence resolves directly to the binding that site introduces. Other occurrences use scope lookup, and a Rust let applies sequential lookup to reference occurrences in its own value, type, and alternative.
